Data science is a collaborative discipline.
Pretty much no data scientist works alone, so neither should you!
In this course you'll collaborate with teammates on the project.

The first milestone of the project, today's activity, will introduce you to the technical aspects of collaborating on a reproducible data science project that is version controlled by Git and hosted on GitHub in a repository shared by all teammates.

Yes, this means you and all of your teammates will be pushing to the same repository!
Sometimes things will go swimmingly, and sometimes you'll run into **merge conflicts**.

::: callout-note
The word "conflict" has a negative connotation.
And, indeed, merge conflicts can be frustrating.
But they serve to make sure no team member inadvertently overwrites another team member's work.
All changes that are in "conflict" with each other need to get resolved explicitly, with a commit message, which helps avoid haphazard overwriting.
:::

# Goals

The goals of this milestone are as follows:

-   Pick a team name
-   Collaborate on GitHub with your teammates and resolve merge conflicts when they inevitably occur
-   Discuss and write up your team contract

# Team name

Pick a team name.
It can be straightforward, or it can be cheeky, but it must be [SFW](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/SFW).
Let your TA know your team name asap.
Once everyone's team names are in, your project repos will be created (give your TA a couple of minutes), and then you can continue with the rest of your task.

# Activity

## Setup

-   Copy the HTTPS URL of your team's project repo from GitHub. In Positron, select *New* ➛ *New Folder From Git...*, paste the URL, and open the cloned repo as your workspace.
-   Open `about.qmd` from the *Explorer* pane.
-   Assign the numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4 to each of the team members. If your team has fewer than 4 people, some people will need to have multiple numbers. Make sure that no team member is assigned consecutive numbers.

### Workflow in Positron

Use these steps whenever the activity asks you to render, stage, commit, push, or pull:

-   **Render and preview:** Save your edits and click *Preview* at the top of the `.qmd` editor to inspect the rendered page in the *Viewer*. To render the entire project website, run `quarto render` in Positron's *Terminal*, from the project folder containing `_quarto.yml`.
-   **Stage:** Open the *Source Control* pane from the Activity bar. Review the changed files, then click the `+` next to each file to stage it. Include the rendered website files as well as the source files. Staged files appear under *Staged Changes*.
-   **Commit:** Enter an informative message in the *Message* box and click *Commit*.
-   **Push:** Open the Command Palette (*View* ➛ *Command Palette...*), search for `Git: Push`, and select it.
-   **Pull:** Open the Command Palette, search for `Git: Pull`, and select it.

::: callout-important
For this exercise, use *Commit*, *Push*, and *Pull* as separate actions, in the order specified below.
Do not use *Sync Changes* or *Commit & Sync*: syncing pulls and pushes together, which would change the sequence of the exercise.
:::

## Let's cause a merge conflict!

Our goal is to see two different types of merges: first, a merge that Git cannot resolve automatically (a **merge conflict**) and that requires human intervention; then, a merge that Git can resolve automatically.

Doing this will require some tight choreography, so pay attention!

Take turns completing the exercise, with only one member working at a time.
**Others should just watch and not do anything in their own projects (this includes not even pulling changes!)** until they are instructed to.
If you feel like you won't be able to resist the urge to touch your computer when it's not your turn, we recommend putting your hands in your pockets or sitting on them!

### Before starting

Everyone should have the repo cloned and know which role number(s) they are.

### Role 1

-   Go to `about.qmd` in your project repo. Change the `[team name]` to your actual team name.
-   Save and click *Preview* to check the page, then render the website with `quarto render` in the *Terminal*.
-   In *Source Control*, stage all changed files and commit them. Then run *Git: Push* from the Command Palette.

::: callout-important
Make sure the previous role has finished before moving on to the next step.
:::

### Role 2

-   Change the team name to some other word.
    Save and click *Preview*, then run `quarto render` in the *Terminal*.
    Stage all changed files in *Source Control* and commit them.

-   Run *Git: Push* from the Command Palette.
    You should get an error because Role 1 has already pushed changes that you do not yet have locally.

-   Run *Git: Pull* from the Command Palette.
    In *Source Control*, look for `about.qmd` under *Merge Changes* and open it in the text editor to inspect the conflict.

    For example, if Role 1 chose "Team Dialectic Blue" and Role 2 changed it to "Team Royal Blue", the conflicting section might look like this:

    ```text
    <<<<<<< HEAD
    This project was developed by Team Royal Blue.
    =======
    This project was developed by Team Dialectic Blue.
    >>>>>>> 97e290f39f197467b5563ea8f81187b760c95aa2
    ```

    The top section contains your local changes; the bottom section contains the changes you pulled from GitHub.
    The string after `>>>>>>>` identifies the incoming commit.

-   Resolve the conflict by editing `about.qmd` to keep the team's preferred name and removing all conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, and `>>>>>>>`).
    Save the file.
    If Positron opens the three-way merge editor, you can choose or edit the result there instead; check the final text before completing the merge.

-   Resolve any conflicts in other source files, then click *Preview* to check the result and run `quarto render` in the *Terminal*.
    If rendered website files also have conflicts, rendering regenerates them from the resolved source files.

-   In *Source Control*, click the `+` next to each resolved file under *Merge Changes*, and stage any remaining changed files under *Changes*.
    Check that *Merge Changes* is empty and that all files you intend to commit appear under *Staged Changes*.

-   Commit with a message describing the resolution, then run *Git: Push* from the Command Palette.
    This time, the push should succeed.

::: callout-tip
If pulling stops with a message about reconciling divergent branches, run `git pull --no-rebase` in Positron's *Terminal* to use a merge for this exercise.
Ask your TA for help if you see a different error or are unsure how to resolve a conflict.
:::

::: callout-important
Make sure the previous role has finished before moving on to the next step.
:::

### Role 3

-   Change the name of the first team member.
-   Save and click *Preview*, then run `quarto render` in the *Terminal*. Stage all changed files in *Source Control*, commit, and run *Git: Push*. You should get an error.
-   Run *Git: Pull*. Since you edited a different part of `about.qmd`, Git should merge that file automatically. If rendered files have conflicts, regenerate them with `quarto render`, stage them, and commit the merge as in Role 2.
-   If *Source Control* still shows a merge waiting to be committed, complete that commit. Then run *Git: Push*.

::: callout-important
Make sure the previous role has finished before moving on to the next step.
:::

### Role 4

-   Change the name of the first team member to something other than what the previous team member did.
-   Save and click *Preview*, then run `quarto render` in the *Terminal*. Stage all changed files in *Source Control*, commit, and run *Git: Push*. You should get an error.
-   Run *Git: Pull*. Resolve the conflicts using the same steps as Role 2: edit and save the source files, preview, render the website, stage the resolved and changed files, commit, and run *Git: Push*.

::: callout-important
Make sure the previous role has finished before moving on to the next step.
:::

### Back to Role 1 (for 4-person teams) or Role 5 (for 5-person teams)

-   Run *Git: Pull* to get all changes from the remote repo.
-   Update all requested pieces of information about all team members.
-   Save and click *Preview*, then run `quarto render` in the *Terminal*. Stage all changed files in *Source Control*, commit, and run *Git: Push*. You should not get an error because you pulled first.
This models "good" collaborative behavior -- start with pulling before doing any work.

### Everyone

Run *Git: Pull*, open `about.qmd`, and click *Preview* to observe the changes in your project.

# Tips for collaborating via GitHub

-   **Always pull first before you start working.**
-   Resolve a merge conflict (edit, save, render, stage, commit, and push) *before* continuing your work. Never do new work while resolving a merge conflict.
-   Preview, stage, commit, and push often to minimize merge conflicts and/or to make merge conflicts easier to resolve.
-   If you find yourself in a situation that is difficult to resolve, ask questions ASAP. Don't let it linger and get bigger.

# Team contract

Team member with Role 2 is the scribe (note taker).

In Positron, run *Git: Pull* to get the latest changes, then open `contract.qmd` from the *Explorer* pane.
Discuss the prompts and write up your answers.
Once done, save and click *Preview*, then run `quarto render` in the *Terminal*.
Stage all changed files in *Source Control*, commit, and run *Git: Push*.

# Team interests

Team member with Role 3 is the scribe now.

In Positron, run *Git: Pull* to get the latest changes, then open `proposal.qmd` from the *Explorer* pane.
Discuss data science topics that interest your team and you might want to pursue finding datasets on.
Briefly summarize your discussion in the appropriate portion of the `proposal.qmd`. document.
Once done, save and click *Preview*, then run `quarto render` in the *Terminal*.
Stage all changed files in *Source Control*, commit, and run *Git: Push*.
